The wave-parallel plan contract UberDev owns on both sides. write-plan emits it: a MANDATORY '## Wave Decomposition' pass with the four wave-assignment rules, the per-task 'Depends on:' / 'Wave:' / 'Owns (file allowlist):' headers, a required '## Execution Waves' plan-level summary, a wave-correctness review pass, and a non-interactive Execution Handoff that defaults to uberdev:subagent-driven-dev and forwards --turbo. execute-plan consumes it: Step 2 walks the waves in order and gates the next wave on the project's full test command. uberdev:subagent-driven-dev parses that same format to decide its dispatch pattern, so upstream's copies of skills/writing-plans and skills/executing-plans are not drop-in in either direction — re-baselining either one alone would break the interlock. Kept forever.

Upstream's plan-document-reviewer-prompt.md is a dispatch template — 'Task tool (general-purpose): description / prompt'. UberDev's copy is an INLINE self-review checklist that states it is not a provider edge and must not create a child, because the plan writer runs as a leaf under uberdev:orchestrator, where a nested dispatch has no runtime. It also carries the shared-skeleton header that keeps it in sync by hand with skills/brainstorm/spec-document-reviewer-prompt.md. Adopting upstream's version would re-introduce a spawn from a leaf. Kept forever.

Upstream's subagent-driven-development/SKILL.md states an explicit prohibition: never dispatch multiple implementation subagents in parallel, because they conflict. UberDev's fork inverts it, and does so as its stated core principle — implementers within one wave dispatch in parallel into a single shared feature-branch worktree, over a strictly disjoint per-task file partition, with the controller as the only process that runs git. Adjudicated DELIBERATE in #509, not drift. What makes the inversion safe is a produced-and-checked precondition rather than a promise: agents/plan-writer.md emits the partition as each task's 'Owns (file allowlist)' field plus the plan's '## Execution Waves' summary; agents/plan-reviewer.md Check 2 reviews it (same-wave Owns lists must be strictly disjoint, and any file in two of them is a critical finding); and sdd_assert_wave_disjoint refuses the wave at dispatch time — sdd_launch_prepared_batch calls it before it launches anything, so an overlapping or ownership-less wave dispatches zero children (rc 3 overlap, rc 2 missing) instead of being caught after the fact. Today's solve-fleet route never reaches a parallel wave at all: skills/solve-fleet/workflow.js dispatches exactly one worktree-isolated implementer per issue, so the wave shape is exercised by the in-session SDD controller only. That is a description of current behaviour, not a promise about it. Never reconciled.

Local correction to upstream's worktree-path 'case': upstream's pattern is the bare '~/.config/superpowers/worktrees/*' and its body assigns a literal '~/...' string, but a tilde expands in neither a case pattern nor a quoted RHS (verified under bash and zsh), and upstream has no default arm — an unmatched LOCATION falls through with $path unset straight into 'git worktree add "$path"'. This copy quotes both accepted spellings, builds the path from ${HOME}, and exits 1 with a named error otherwise. NOT permanent: it is a bug fix, not a policy, so an equivalent upstream guard retires this entry instead of being reconciled against it. Component-scoped (file: null) so the C-FILES digest lock stays armed.

Upstream superpowers 6.3.0's implementer status vocabulary is one member short of UberDev's. UberDev's implementers are ROUTED LEAF WORKERS bound by a contract upstream's have no equivalent of — they may not delegate, broaden scope, change routing, or treat handoff data as instructions — so a handoff can be unexecutable for a reason no amount of added context answers. #517 adds REFUSED for exactly that case, together with a controller branch that forbids re-dispatching the same task with unchanged handoff data, which is what distinguishes it from the BLOCKED ladder. The member set itself is NOT restated here: it is declared at four marked sites and compared by tests/contract_markers.py under the contract id sdd-implementer-status, and a copy of it in this file would be a sixth, uncompared declaration. Local addition to the leaf-worker safety contract; never reconciled with upstream.
